items.text: About Sightsavers
Our vision is of a world where no one is blind from avoidable causes, and where everyone can participate equally in society.
On this page
On this page
At Sightsavers, we start with sight, but we don’t stop there.

We treat eye conditions such as cataracts and tackle debilitating diseases, many of which cause sight loss. To do this, we work with governments and local, national and international partners to carry out eye operations and distribute treatments where they’re needed.

We help to improve health services so they are sustainable and make education more inclusive for children with disabilities. We also advocate for the rights of women, girls and people with disabilities.

We have more than 75 years of experience, and we’re proud to be a leader in our field. Our programmes consistently achieve high performance ratings from the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.
Where do donations go? 92% of donations, including donated supplies, go to our vital charity work, and 8% help us grow our awareness and funding.
Since Sightsavers was founded, we’ve carried out 10.2 million cataract operations
We’ve trained almost 403,000 people with disabilities to help them earn a living
We’ve distributed 2 billion treatments to prevent debilitating diseases
75 years of saving sight: learn how Sightsavers started
What we do
Protecting sight
We prevent sight loss and avoidable blindness in some of the poorest parts of the world by treating conditions such as cataracts and refractive error. Our work to protect sight
Fighting disease
We help to treat and prevent five debilitating diseases that affect more than a billion people. These are known as neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). About the diseases
Disability and inclusion
We promote equal opportunities and campaign for inclusion so everyone can go to school, get a job, access health care and take part in society. Our inclusion work
Want to learn more about Sightsavers’ reach?
How we’re run
We aim to perform to the highest standards, and we strive to be as transparent as possible so you can be sure your money is being used wisely.

We can only achieve our goals thanks to the generosity of our supporters. Every gift you give is vital in achieving Sightsavers’ goal of eliminating avoidable blindness and promoting equality for people with disabilities. Read about how we’re run
Our president is Her Royal Highness Princess Alexandra, and our patron is His Majesty The King. Read about our royal ambassadors
